evidence.text: Two spoons 匕 side-by-side; 匕 also provides the pronunciation
Pictograph of two people side-by-side, conveying the meaning "to put together", "match", or "compare".
密也。二人爲从，反从爲比。凡比之屬皆从比。

Chu Wan-li (1948): Phonetic compound (OC *piʔ, *pis, *bi, *bis, *biɡ): phonetic 匕 (OC *pilʔ) + phonetic 匕 (OC *pilʔ).
Shuowen: Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 人 (“man”) + 人 – to juxtapose.
Similar but unrelated to 从, 尼, 化 and 北.
Perhaps from a Proto-Sino-Tibetan *phi-r/n/s (“late, behind, after, outside”) (STEDT root #5883). Cognate with 頻 (OC *bin, “several in succession”); outside of Sinitic, compare Proto-Naga *pʰaːy (“after”), as well as possibly Burmese ပြင် (prang, “outside”).
密也。二人爲从，反从爲比。凡比之屬皆从比。

evidence.source: Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica (Sinica database)
evidence.text: The catalog record identifies 屈萬里, “甲骨文从比二字辨,” published in 1948 in Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology 13, pp. 213–217. The record was found, but opening the page returned an internal error; its argument was not verified from the article itself.
evidence.title: 史語所集刊｜中央研究院歷史語言研究所

evidence.text: A report on Lin Yun’s 2016 lecture says Lin distinguished 比 from 从 in oracle-bone forms and syntax, argued that 比 derives from 匕-like forms rather than the person-sign analysis in Shuowen, and read 王比某伐某方 as alliance or joining in warfare. The report presents Lin’s interpretation, not consensus proof of every graph or lexical relationship.
evidence.title: 傅斯年讲座︱林沄：神权、军权与族权，商王最重视哪个权力

evidence.source: Li Zongkun, Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: In a 2007 article abstract on the Shang divination phrase 王比望乘, Li reports competing readings: earlier scholars took 比 as follow or lead, others understood it as close alliance, while Li argues it means assist or support—potentially supplying personnel and materials for a campaign. The example is an early Shang use, but its exact sense remains disputed.
evidence.title: 卜辭中的「望乘」——兼釋「比」的辭意

evidence.source: 金真姬, 常用漢字二百字探源
evidence.text: The study presents forms labeled Shang, Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States, and clerical, with cited examples including oracle-bone collection numbers 合集 27578, 34268, 32555, 27926 and Western Zhou vessels 比簋 and 班簋. It reports multiple Shang shapes and a continuing basic structure with later added strokes and graphic variation. Its discussion also notes that 比 and 从 forms can be confused and that interpretations should be tested against inscription contexts. This supports a sequence of attested shapes, not a single certain pictographic analysis.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.source: Xu Shen, Shuowen Jiezi, 比部 (Chinese Text Project transcription)
evidence.text: The Han dictionary account glosses 比 as “密也” and analyzes it as two 人 forms, with the reversed 从 form becoming 比. This is an important historical analysis, but its interpretation is not independently confirmed by the early-script evidence reviewed here.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷九 : 比部

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, accessed through Kotobank
evidence.text: This dictionary describes 比 as two people side by side and distinguishes its orientation from 从; it reports 比助 uses in bronze inscriptions and relates the meanings ‘compare,’ ‘associate/follow,’ and ‘be close.’ This is a dictionary’s analysis and gloss sequence, not evidence that the semantic extensions occurred in that order.
evidence.title: 比（読み）ヒ｜普及版 字通

evidence.text: Their 2014 Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese table gives 比, modern Mandarin bǐ, Middle Chinese pjijX, Old Chinese *C.pijʔ, glossed ‘compare’; it separately lists 比 bì with *pij-s ‘combine; all’. This shows that 比 has multiple reconstructed readings and senses in this system.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.text: The same Baxter–Sagart table lists 匕 bǐ with Middle Chinese pjijX and Old Chinese *pijʔ, glossed ‘ladle, spoon’ and ‘spoon’. Compared with 比 *C.pijʔ, the forms are similar in this reconstruction system. This sound correspondence alone does not show that the early graph 比 was composed of two spoon graphs, nor does it establish that its depicted referent was a spoon.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Zhengzhang system table, accessed through Wiktionary
evidence.text: The entry reports Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003 reconstructions 比 *piʔ and 匕 *pilʔ. In that system too the forms are similar, though not identical. These are reconstructions, not direct recordings of pronunciation.
evidence.title: 比 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Xu Shen, Shuowen Jiezi, 匕部, with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: Shuowen describes 匕 as a sign associated with ordering or arranging together and also as a utensil used to take food; Duan Yucai’s note treats the food-taking utensil sense as the one that became current. This supports an old dictionary association of 匕 with a food utensil, but does not establish the pictured object’s exact historical pronunciation independently of reconstructions.
evidence.title: 說文解字「匕」

evidence.source: The Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry records variant forms and says some variant relations rely on Shuowen, Yupian, Jiyun, and Kangxi references; it notes uncertainty about the provenance of one form and a possible Kangxi/Yupian error. The entry lists oracle-bone and bronze paleography collections, but their relevant images are marked unavailable. It therefore does not independently settle 比’s earliest graph analysis.
evidence.title: [A02102] 比 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project transcription of the Analects
evidence.text: The Analects, Wei Zheng chapter, includes 君子周而不比，小人比而不周. This is a classical attestation of 比 in a context conventionally interpreted as partial association or factional attachment. The page was returned in search but could not be opened because access returned 403.
evidence.title: 論語 : 為政

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project transcription of Zhouyi commentary
evidence.text: The Zhouyi commentary text gives 比，輔也, ‘比 is to assist/support,’ an attested classical gloss. The page was returned in search but opening it returned 403.
evidence.title: 周易注 : 上經需傳卷二比

evidence.source: Wikisource transcription of Shijing, Xiaoya, 六月
evidence.text: The poem includes 比物四骊, in a passage about matching or arranging a team of four black horses. The transmitted poem is conventionally assigned to the Western Zhou period, but the inspected page gives no independently established date for this particular written witness. The context attests a use involving matching or ordering; it does not by itself establish when that sense arose.
evidence.title: 诗经/六月

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project / Zhouli text reproduced by Gushiji
evidence.text: The Zhouli passage 凡礼事，赞小宰比官府之具 uses 比 in an administrative context of checking or arranging official supplies. The textual page labels the work pre-Qin but does not establish the date of this wording; the received Zhouli text cannot be used as a precise chronological marker without further textual-history evidence.
evidence.title: 《周礼》天官冢宰·宰夫

evidence.source: Hong Kong Education Bureau, Chinese Language Learning and Teaching resource, 字源考釋
evidence.text: The entry displays a sequence labeled oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and standard forms, and describes the early forms as two closely adjacent people facing right. This is the resource's graphic analysis, not independent proof that the forms depict people.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 比

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen account 密也。二人為从，反从為比 and lists three modern Mandarin readings: bì, bǐ, and pí. It indexes historical dictionary and paleographic collections, but marks the oracle-bone, bronze, and ancient-character volumes unavailable online. The cited text is an inherited dictionary analysis, not an independent paleographic demonstration.
evidence.title: [A02102] 比 - 教育部《異體字字典》 臺灣學術網路十四版（正式七版）2024

evidence.text: The 2014 Baxter–Sagart table lists 比 bǐ with Middle Chinese pjijX and Old Chinese *C.pijʔ, glossed ‘compare’; it separately lists 比 bì with pjijH and *pij-s, glossed ‘combine; all’. These are distinct reconstructed readings and glosses in this system.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.text: The same table lists 匕 bǐ with Middle Chinese pjijX and Old Chinese *pijʔ, glossed ‘ladle, spoon’ or ‘spoon’. In this reconstruction system its forms are similar to 比 *C.pijʔ. That similarity alone does not establish that 匕 is a phonetic component in 比, or that an object pictured by 比 was a spoon.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons file description and licensing page
evidence.text: This is a modern vector chart comparing selected late Shang bronze and oracle-script forms with modern characters. Its description enumerates 天、犬、旅、何、父、戈、正、韋, not 比, so it does not directly illustrate 比 and is not proposed as a 比 glyph candidate. The uploader dedicated the file under CC0 1.0.
evidence.title: File:Shang Bronze and Oracle Script.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The search result surfaced this oracle-bone specimen, dated in its Commons description to the Shang period and linked to British Library Or.7694/1595 verso. Its description concerns a lunar-eclipse/calendar inscription and does not identify a 比 graph; it is a historical artifact photograph, but not a supported character-specific candidate.
evidence.title: File:Oracle bone from the Couling-Chalfant collection.jpg - Wikimedia Commons

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: Early oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions were not visually inspected in this research, and the Sinica oracle-bone query database was not successfully queried for individual 比 entries.
The Sinica bibliographic record for Qu Wanli’s 1948 article was found, but the article page could not be opened; its detailed evidence and reasoning therefore remain unchecked here.

The early graph’s component analysis remains disputed: Shuowen and person-like analyses conflict with 匕-based readings. Available evidence did not establish that 比 was formed from two spoon-signs, or resolve whether the relevant early sign depicted a person or another referent.

The sound match between 匕 and 比 is supported by Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang reconstructions, but reconstructed similarity does not by itself prove a phonetic-component role; neither reconstruction recovers a spoken name for any object allegedly depicted in 比.

The exact semantic relation from early Shang 比 in 王比望乘 to ‘associate/assist,’ ‘juxtapose,’ and ‘compare’ is not established. The Shang phrase itself has competing readings, and dictionary gloss ordering cannot establish chronology.

Classical texts provide attestations in contexts such as comparison or arrangement, partial association, and assistance, but this search did not establish dated manuscript witnesses or a chronological chain among these senses.
The Shuowen small-seal and ancient-form images were not visually examined. The Ministry of Education entry identifies source collections but reports relevant paleographic images unavailable.
No evidence was found for whole-graph borrowing as the origin of 比; the phonetic proposal concerns a sound component within the graph, and remains disputed against semantic or pictographic analyses.

The inspected external sources did not establish a consensus formation analysis for 比. The person-like interpretation is explicitly an educational resource and Shuowen's account; the dossier also records a competing 匕-based proposal and scholarly dispute. Early inscription images were not independently checked character by character in this browsing stage.

The 匕–比 pronunciation similarity is supported here only within the Baxter–Sagart reconstruction system; it does not itself establish phonetic-component status. The sound or name of any alleged depicted object is not independently recoverable from this evidence.

No inspected source supplied a securely dated earliest attestation plus a chronological semantic chain. Separate early Shang and classical semantic debates in the supplied dossier remain unresolved; gloss ordering is not evidence of development order.

Commons searches found historical oracle-bone artifact photographs and modern redrawings, but not a direct 比 glyph image whose identity, original paleographic source, and reuse provenance were all established. Therefore no historical glyph candidate is proposed. The Commons general chart is a modern drawing and does not include 比.
The Shuowen.org 匕 page opened without extractable text in this web inspection, so its content was not independently verified here.

limitations.text: No candidate could be confirmed as an image of 比 with a reliable source identity and reuse rights. The available oracle-bone chart omits 比, and the surfaced artifact photographs do not identify a 比 inscription.
